R01.title: Degree and subject equivalence
R01.proposed_interpretation: Compare supplied totals only in the published unit; compare student-confirmed course allocations as entered facts. Resolve equivalence only from the exact published reference qualification or an explicitly reported university assessment. A matching degree title does not certify equivalence. Routine committee-selection wording alone adds no extra hard blocker.
R01.unresolved: No automatic non-ECTS conversion or semantic course assignment. Degree duration, completion, module content and required university assessments must remain explicit.

R02.title: KIT CS: selection alternatives and separate GRE condition
R02.proposed_interpretation: Use degree prerequisites AND the applicable GRE/GATE condition AND any_of(full 15/30/8/25 credits, qualifying GATE CS/DA, passed interview). Interview eligibility needs at least three of the relaxed 15/20/6/20 areas and top-10% evidence from the admission page. Invitation alone does not pass the interview. Rank is not universal.
R02.unresolved: Programme text says regulations are subject to approval; department shorthand says international applicants. Review the dated regulation and reconcile scope before treating the draft as an approved machine rule. Do not merge the admission-route and GRE-alternative groups.

R03.title: KIT CDS: grouped credits, thesis and conditional admission
R03.proposed_interpretation: Require basic maths 20 LP plus 40 LP in one of three domains and 12 LP in each other domain, and a thesis/comparable independent scientific work of at least 6 LP. Up to 12 missing LP can lead to discretionary conditional admission, with completion within the first three semesters; it is not an unconditional pass.
R03.unresolved: The cached page does not establish an overlap/double-counting policy for basic maths versus domain credits or thesis credits. Do not invent disjointness or allow double counting without evidence. Missing thesis is a material extraction omission; retain a correction candidate until Save review. Conditional approval remains university review.

R04.title: KIT test validity and accepted English proof
R04.proposed_interpretation: GRE no older than five years; GATE no older than three, using a reviewed reference date. English proof is an any_of group with overall AND components inside each test, education-based routes, and proof due by enrolment. KIT explicitly accepts its listed English tests without time limit.
R04.unresolved: Check the reference date and inclusive age boundary for GRE/GATE; do not copy a generic two-year English validity rule. Cambridge names alone do not publish a numeric pass score. KIT CDS omits the education routes from its record; attach supplemental evidence pending correction review.

R05.title: RWTH: country basis and strict GRE bounds
R05.proposed_interpretation: CS uses qualifying-degree country outside the EU. DS exempts EU/EEA citizens or German secondary-school qualifiers. Otherwise QR >75th percentile AND VR >15th percentile AND AW >=3.5. Preserve percentile identity, strict boundaries and DS submission with the application.
R05.unresolved: Unknown citizenship/degree/school facts or unresolved country-group membership cannot imply exemption. CS degree-country exemptions cannot be reused for DS.

R06.title: Country-group definitions need independent official evidence
R06.proposed_interpretation: Version EU, EEA, EHEA and relevant Lisbon-signatory groups separately, with effective date and official membership evidence. Programme citations establish which group applies, not the membership list.
R06.unresolved: Official membership lists are not in the current registry. Collect and review them in Step 3; do not populate from model memory. Preserve Saarland non-EHEA branch-campus handling.

R07.title: RWTH English scope and milestone
R07.proposed_interpretation: PDF programme rows point CS and DS to section 3(9), while the parsed PDF contains two English-score lists. CS also needs accepted German proof at enrolment; DS explicitly requires no German. English proof is due at enrolment according to application guidance.
R07.unresolved: Confirm the visual PDF section-to-score mapping and accepted certificate/exemption scope before enabling a positive language verdict. Retain both lists as evidence; do not choose 90/6.0 merely because the current record does.

R08.title: Darmstadt: competencies and conditional exam, both programmes
R08.proposed_interpretation: Academic equivalence (180 total and 60 matching core ECTS) remains separate from formal exam outcomes. Trigger the entrance exam only when document review cannot confirm competencies. Qualifying GRE (155/165/3.5, same sitting, no compensation) OR GATE overall >=750 can exempt the exam, with August 20/February 20 submission deadlines.
R08.unresolved: GRE is not universally mandatory and does not independently certify degree equivalence. Missing assessment is unknown. The CS flat one_of record needs explicit source-faithful interpretation; do not silently edit it. AIML documents are not_published in its record although the shared guide supplies prerequisites.

R09.title: Saarland: grade alternatives AND class rank
R09.proposed_interpretation: Interpret the published threshold as (75% OR 3.00/4 on the applicable original scale) AND top-10% class rank. Compare original scales only; do not convert 75% to a German cutoff or require both grade scales.
R09.unresolved: Keep subject-competency/foreign-degree equivalence review separately from the numeric comparison. Contradictory grade evidence needs review.

R10.title: Saarland: test submission and English exceptions
R10.proposed_interpretation: Outside the degree-region exemptions require GRE General OR Indian GATE result, with no invented numeric minimum. English tests can be home editions or expired; MOI alone is disallowed. Native-speaker/in-person-education exceptions require the stated countries and documentary evidence. German-school evidence is individually examined.
R10.unresolved: Do not infer exemption from citizenship alone, a remote degree, or the parent institution of a non-EHEA branch campus. The record associates 2026 TOEFL wording with PBT as well as iBT: keep formats distinct and review that ambiguous scope.

R11.title: Deadlines: years, routes, classes and exceptions
R11.proposed_interpretation: Use intake starting year Y and an explicit offset for every date. Offset -1: RWTH summer September; Saarland winter early November and summer early May/final November; Dresden foreign-degree non-EU summer November; TUM final summer November and Informatics recommended summer October; Stuttgart final summer July. Offset 0: the other listed winter deadlines and summer January deadlines, plus Darmstadt summer February test-exemption submission. KIT CS summer January is 0. Keep closing days inclusive.
R11.unresolved: RWTH current-enrolment/relevant-German-degree exceptions change deadlines, and DS explicitly names EEA. Separate Dresden aptitude-registration from uni-assist application; TUM Informatics recommended visa dates from final dates; Darmstadt hard-copy arrival and August20/February20 test-exemption submission from application. TUM assessment dates can be semester-specific, not recurring. TU Berlin/KIT CDS have no numeric application deadline in their verified records; do not borrow siblings.

R12.title: TU Berlin: credit exclusions and proof/route scope
R12.proposed_interpretation: 36 foundations CP contains the three 12-CP areas, plus 18 maths and 30 additional CS excluding thesis; do not count the 36 and its children twice. Theoretical-CS exclusions apply. Faculty IV IELTS >=6.5 and its listed degree-country proof route apply; generic B2 or MOI elsewhere does not suffice. Foreign-degree VPD applies from summer 2026, alongside the university application.
R12.unresolved: Other Faculty IV accepted certificates and the numeric application deadline are linked but not captured fully in the current cache. Keep those branches unresolved. All academic allocation equivalence remains the board decision.

R13.title: Dresden: test format and separate aptitude procedure
R13.proposed_interpretation: Accepted TOEFL old-format 95 or new-format 5.0, or IELTS 7.0, must be represented as actual evidence identities, not a generic C1 claim. German-degree applicants have a separate aptitude-registration portal/window; foreign-degree applications use uni-assist with applicant-class dates. University aptitude remains a required assessment.
R13.unresolved: The new TOEFL score is omitted in the record; record a correction candidate. Do not treat not_published entrance_tests as absence of the aptitude prerequisite, which is stated under selection_process. Resolve class terminology without silently assuming EU means EEA.

R14.title: TUM: English omission, optional documents and assessment
R14.proposed_interpretation: English evidence is required by the application deadline for both programmes even though english is not_published in the records. GRE 164 QR AND 4.0 AW OR qualifying annual CS GATE applies by degree country (Bangladesh, China, India, Iran, Pakistan); VPD and APS have separate degree-country predicates. Optional training certificates stay optional. The university aptitude assessment is distinct from GRE/GATE.
R14.unresolved: The cached language-certificates page contains German proof, not the complete English thresholds. Obtain the official English-proof evidence before automating that branch. Programme overview describes an interview while department text describes a second-stage test: keep unresolved review and period-specific dates, including the 2026-only test. No fabricated aptitude point formula. Updated 2026-11-12: the English thresholds are now in both verified records (de/tum/language-certificates, read after the parser fix); the rest of this review is unchanged and still pending.

R15.title: Stuttgart: language validity and conditional assessment
R15.proposed_interpretation: IELTS Academic >=7; TOEFL 95 old scale or >=5 new scale; other specifically named certificates. Certificate validity must extend to the deadline; do not universally assign two years where the source says most certificates. MOI is not accepted. Native-country exception requires citizenship AND education, with Canada excluding Quebec. Missing qualifications can require an interview/exam or discretionary conditions.
R15.unresolved: The level/duration of education for the exception is not fully specified. Keep ambiguous education evidence and conditional admission as review; do not infer automatic eligibility or rejection from an invitation.

R16.title: Documents, APS and readiness remain separate
R16.proposed_interpretation: Use degree-country APS rules where published, conditional VPD/GRE/language documents, ongoing-degree evidence and required milestones. Not_published APS does not mean exempt. Missing documents, pending submission and late application go to readiness, not an academic-failure headline. Lists are not asserted exhaustive.
R16.unresolved: Unlisted APS/programme-country combinations need sourced evidence; do not import nationality-based conditions. Shared-source document omissions (KIT CDS, Darmstadt AIML) are visible correction candidates, not silent normalisation.

R17.title: Fees, financial proof and source periods
R17.proposed_interpretation: Display fees as cited information with scope/period and possible exemptions. Darmstadt EUR348.18 is labelled summer 2025; Dresden EUR361 is winter 2026/27. Do not certify future fees, waivers or visa funding from citizenship or a bank balance alone. Financial proof is a separate purpose/period/route comparison.
R17.unresolved: Review separate national funds evidence and official grade-conversion evidence in Step 2/3. No universal visa amount or grade cutoff is introduced by this inventory. Expired fee periods remain visible.
